 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 22 09-05-2025 I.A. No. 1 of 2025 1.
Heard Mr. Sanjay Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. Sanjay Kumar Jha, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2 and Mr. Syed Ashfaque Ahmad, learned APP for the State.

2. The instant interlocutory application has been placed for consideration of appellant's prayer for suspension of his sentence and his release on bail under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short 'Cr. P.C').
3.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 10.01.2022 and order of sentence dated 13.01.2022 passed by the Court of learned Additional District & Sessions Judge VI-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: Mr. Sanjay Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that this is the second attempt of the appellant to get the relief under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. and his first prayer was rejected by this court vide order dated 05.09.2023 giving him a liberty to renew his prayer after one year from the date of that order on this condition if his appeal is not taken up for hearing in the said period and now, the appellant has renewed his prayer mainly in the light of this liberty as well as his long incarceration period in jail which has been about 5 years, 3 months and 8 days and secondly,
there is little chance of an early hearing of the appellant's appeal as it relates to the year 2022.

It is further submitted that the FIR was lodged after an inordinate delay of five days and there was a property dispute between the appellant and victim's father during the relevant period of the alleged occurrence which was accepted by two prosecution witnesses who went hostile.
5. On the other hand, Mr. Sanjay Kumar Jha, learned Patna High Court CR.
APP ( SJ) No.536 of 2022(22) dt.09-05-2025 counsel for the respondent no. 2

, has vehemently opposed the prayer of the appellant and submits that the appellant is own uncle of the victim and he raped the victim when she and her younger brother were alone in their house taking advantage of that vulnerable situation

and in view of the nature of allegation, the appellant does not deserve to any relief under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C.
6.

Learned APP appearing for the State has also opposed the prayer of the appellant and submits that in this matter, written objection has been filed to the present interlocutory application and the same may be perused and there is serious allegation against the appellant.
7. Heard both the sides and perused the relevant materials.

Though, against the appellant there is serious allegation, however, considering his present custody period which has been 5 years, 3 months and 8 days as stated above and also unlikelihood of his appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future as the same relates to the year 2022, in my opinion, now, the appellant deserves to the relief under Section 389(1) of the Cr. P.C. Accordingly, let the appellant named-above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.536 of 2022(22) dt.09-05-2025 with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge VI-cum- Special Judge (POCSO), Banka in Connection with Katoriya P.S. Case No. 13 of 2020 (G.R. No. 12 of 2020).
8.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sentence of imprisonment awarded upon the appellant shall remain suspended during his bail period.
9. In result, I.A. No. 1 of 2025 stands allowed.

(Shailendra Singh, J) Rajiv/-
